sources.origin: Wikipedia "Jefferson nickel" infobox (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_nickel, revision 1383232384), "Wartime Nickels (mid-1942 to 1945)": 56% copper, 35% silver, 9% manganese; mass 5.000 g and diameter 21.21 mm as the copper-nickel coins; composition cross-checked against the "Wartime Composition" table caption of the saved source
sources.note: Thickness is not set: no cited source gives it.

rules-note: Business strikes only: proofs (including the S and W proof and reverse-proof rows) are skipped, and collector-only strikes are dropped: 1994 P (167,703) and 1997 P (25,000) "Special Frosted Matte Uncirculated ... collector's sets" and 2017 S (223,310) "Enhanced Uncirculated". Mint marks are as in the source's Mint cell: a Mint cell in parentheses ((P), (P/D/S)) means the coin has no mark (null); a plain letter is the mark. Mintages come only from the saved source; nothing is summed or estimated. This file holds the 1942-1945 wartime silver alloy nickels (56% copper, 35% silver, 9% manganese), the "Wartime Composition" rows of the source, split from the copper-nickel file so the file-level specs fit every coin. 1942 has both compositions: the P and S coins here are the wartime alloy, the 1942 no-mark and D coins are copper-nickel (us-nickels-jefferson-copper-nickel.json). The wartime coins carry the large mint mark above Monticello, including P for Philadelphia, so P is a real mark here (not null). No variety is set: the four 1942 keys differ by mint mark. No cited source names a wartime coin as a key date.
name: Jefferson Nickel
